public_rationale: On SAP's July 23 call, an analyst questioned whether AI token costs contributed to rising R&D spending. The call reported revenue growth below the cited R&D cost growth, and management connected the cost increase to token consumption. This supports the ordinary reading that investor scrutiny would begin. It does not establish widespread rejection of AI spending or that tokens caused the entire cost increase.
limitations: Support depends on treating investment-analyst questions as investor scrutiny and slower relative revenue growth as the trigger.
The call is available through third-party transcript reproductions; the official pages could not be read.
Management also reported productivity benefits and other causes of higher costs. Those qualifications do not negate the occurrence of scrutiny.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Investors will eventually question mounting R&D costs from AI token burn when companies' revenue growth fails to follow.
conditions: when revenue growth fails to follow

statement.excerpt: At some point investors — even the braindead fuckwits who have been inflating the AI bubble — will begin to question mounting R&D costs (which is where AI token burn is usually hidden) when the company’s revenue growth fails to follow.

from_speaker: will begin to question mounting R&D costs
when the company’s revenue growth fails to follow
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that investors will start scrutinizing rising R&D spending that includes internal AI token costs when revenue growth does not keep pace with that spending.
Questions from investment analysts on earnings calls count as public investor scrutiny, consistent with the surrounding reference to an earnings call.
Begin to question requires an identifiable instance of scrutiny, not proof of a market-wide investor revolt.
Revenue growth need not be negative; it must lag the relevant cost growth.
This grades the forecast of scrutiny, not the separate parenthetical generalization about where token costs are usually recorded.
criteria.support_condition: A dated post-publication earnings call or investor communication shows scrutiny of rising R&D costs including AI token costs at a company whose revenue growth lagged that spending.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event rules out such eventual scrutiny. A period without questions, or management defending its spending, cannot falsify this undated forecast.

evidence.locator: Christian Klein's opening remarks; read together with Michael Briest's R&D question and Klein's response
evidence.publisher: SAP earnings call, reproduced by Stock Analysis
evidence.explanation: The same call reports 11% total revenue growth and an analyst's observation of 14% R&D cost growth. Management identifies token consumption in R&D as contributing to the cost increase, satisfying the stated reading of the trigger.

evidence.locator: Q&A, Michael Briest of UBS, immediately after his question about token costs
evidence.publisher: SAP earnings call, reproduced by Stock Analysis
evidence.explanation: Briest asks whether token costs enter R&D and contribute to its increase after noting rising R&D costs. This is an identifiable investment-analyst question about the spending described in the forecast.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: A dated investment-analyst question addresses token costs within rising R&D spending after the same company's reported revenue growth lagged the cited cost growth.
